theory.intro: Three benchmark percentages have quick mental shortcuts because they are simple fractions.
steps: Match the percentage to its fraction ($50\% = \tfrac12$, $25\% = \tfrac14$, $10\% = \tfrac{1}{10}$).
For more than one part, find each amount. Add for a total, subtract from the whole for a remainder, or compare the amounts.

workedExamples.question_text:
Find these benchmark percentages.
(a) $10\%$ of $87$ L.
(b) $25\%$ of $\$86$.
(c) $50\%$ of $7.4$ kg.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $10\%$ is one tenth.
$87\div10=8.7\text{ L}$.
(b) $25\%$ is one quarter. Halve, then halve again.
$86\div2=43$ and $43\div2=21.50$.
So $25\%$ of $\$86$ is $\$21.50$.
(c) $50\%$ is one half.
$7.4\div2=3.7\text{ kg}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Two pieces are cut from an $82$ m roll of ribbon: one is $50\%$ of the roll and the other is $25\%$ of the roll.
(a) Find the total length used.
(b) Find the length remaining.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$50\%\text{ of }82=82\div2=41\text{ m}$.
$25\%\text{ of }82=82\div4=20.5\text{ m}$.
(a) Total used $=41+20.5=61.5\text{ m}$.
(b) Length remaining $=82-61.5=20.5\text{ m}$.
Half and a quarter have been used, so one quarter remains.

workedExamples.question_text:
Compare $25\%$ of $230$ mL with $50\%$ of $96$ mL.
(a) Which amount is greater?
(b) By how much?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$25\%\text{ of }230=230\div4=57.5\text{ mL}$.
$50\%\text{ of }96=96\div2=48\text{ mL}$.
(a) $57.5>48$, so $25\%$ of $230$ mL is greater.
(b) Difference $=57.5-48=9.5\text{ mL}$.

mastery.question_text:
Which is greater: $25\%$ of a $360$-piece collection or $50\%$ of a $140$-piece collection?
By how many pieces?
mastery.solution_text:
$25\%\text{ of }360=360\div4=90$
$50\%\text{ of }140=140\div2=70$
$90-70$
$=20$
$25\%$ of the $360$-piece collection is greater by $20$ pieces.
